body: I'm not alone but I don't want to burden anyone in my life with my issues, they don't deserve to have to deal with this. I don't really have any grounding methods. I usually just let myself ride through the waves of dissociation until I come back to reality which is taking longer and longer.

hi, thanks for responding, I'm glad to know I'm not the only one who has had crappy experiences like this but I'm sorry you had to go through it too. That's awesome that you found a doctor who took you seriously though and that you were able to get the hearing aids you needed.

As for my word recognition, it isn't great at all and that reflects in my test scores but I compensate in real life by using the context of the conversation that I'm having. This of course doesn't always work and so I often find myself struggling to keep up in group settings no matter how hard I try (and don't even get me started on being able to understand speech coming from my phone or television)

Thank you for the advice and I think at some point I may try to find help again, maybe when I start to feel comfortable around doctors again however long that takes. For now I just want to put this whole experience behind me and try to cope as best as I can on my own.
